howItWorks.title: How our matching works
howItWorks.intro: We believe you should be able to see how a match is made. Below you'll find exactly which factors count, how much they weigh and what we never use.

layerA.title: Layer 1 – hard requirements (knock-outs)
layerA.intro: First we check your hard requirements. If a job falls outside them, we hide it by default – with an explanation. You can always choose to show it anyway. Missing data never excludes a job.

rules.sponsorship: Need sponsorship? Then we only show jobs from IND recognised sponsors, and only if the salary meets the highly skilled migrant threshold (from €{norm} gross per month, depending on your situation).
rules.language: If the job requires a language at a certain level (CEFR), we compare it with your level.
rules.location: Your maximum travel time and preference for on-site, hybrid or remote work.
rules.salary: Your minimum salary, if the job states a salary.
rules.contract: Contract type and hours per week.
rules.education: Only when the job explicitly requires a degree. Education never earns bonus points.

layerB.title: Layer 2 – weighted score (0-100)
layerB.intro: Jobs that pass layer 1 get a score on six factors. When information is missing, we redistribute its weight over the other factors and show that.

components.skills: Overlap with the requested skills using the European ESCO standard. Required skills count double, recently used skills weigh more.
components.experience: How similar your previous roles and tasks are to this job in content. Not the number of years.
components.occupation: Distance between occupational groups (ESCO/ISCO) and whether the level fits.
components.interests: Congruence between your interest profile (RIASEC, O*NET Interest Profiler) and the occupation.
components.values: How well the work fits what matters to you (six work values).
components.practical: Salary, commute, remote work, hours and type of organisation.

howItWorks.labels: Labels: Strong match from {strong}, Good match from {good}, Possible match from {possible}.

never.title: What we never use
never.text: Name, age or date of birth, gender, photo, nationality, address or marital status. Your CV is stripped of name, contact details, address and date of birth before processing. An automated test verifies that these attributes never change the outcome.

control.title: You stay in control
control.text: We never reject you automatically. You see all reasons, can show hidden jobs anyway, edit your data and delete your account at any time. Every calculation is logged with the model version used.

science.title: Scientific basis
science.text: We use the European Commission's ESCO taxonomy for skills and occupations, the O*NET Interest Profiler (public domain) for interests and the O*NET work values. We deliberately use no personality or cognitive tests.

free.a: No, JobMatch is free for job seekers.

sponsor.a: Employers recognised by the IND (Dutch immigration service) may sponsor highly skilled migrants. If you need sponsorship, we show only their jobs by default, and only if the salary meets the threshold.

data.q: Which data do you use for matching?
data.a: Your skills, work experience, languages, work status, preferences, interest profile and work values. Nothing else.

photo.q: Why don't you ask for a photo, age or nationality?
photo.a: Because they say nothing about how well you fit a job and can lead to discrimination. We only ask whether you need sponsorship and which residence document you hold.

cv.a: Your CV is stored encrypted in the EU. Before processing we remove your name, contact details, address and date of birth. You can delete earlier versions at any time.

score.a: In two layers: hard requirements (knock-outs) and a weighted score on six factors. All weights are listed on 'How our matching works'.

reject.a: No. We make no automated decisions about you. You always see why a job is hidden and can show it anyway.

delete.q: How do I delete my account?
delete.a: In the Privacy centre you can download all your data or delete your account including all data. We delete inactive accounts after 12 months, after an e-mail warning.

rights.text: Access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability (JSON export in the Privacy centre) and objection. You can also lodge a complaint with the Dutch Data Protection Authority (Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens).

system.title: What the system does
system.text: JobMatch ranks job vacancies for job seekers based on skills, experience, occupation, interests, work values and practical preferences, and explains every match.

riskClass.title: Risk classification
riskClass.text: Because the system is used in the context of employment, we treat it as a high-risk AI system under the EU AI Act and apply the corresponding requirements on data quality, transparency, human oversight, logging and robustness.

data.title: Which data
data.text: Only work-related data. Name, age, gender, photo and nationality are never used; CV text is stripped of identifying details before analysis.

logic.title: How it works
logic.text: A combination of hard requirements and a weighted score, as described on 'How our matching works'. A language model (Claude) helps to read CVs and job ads; the score itself is calculated with transparent, tested rules.

oversight.title: Human oversight
oversight.text: There are no automated rejections. Users see the reasons and can show hidden jobs anyway. Administrators can only change weights by creating a new, logged model version.

logging.title: Logging
logging.text: Every match calculation is recorded with a hash of its input and the model version used, so outcomes are reproducible.

limitations.title: Limitations
limitations.text: Reading CVs and job ads can contain errors, which is why you review your skills yourself. Travel times are estimates. A score is a tool, not a judgement about you.
